summary.headline: IndoStar Q4 FY26 net loss of INR424 crores on INR326 crores extra SR provision and INR49 crores West Asia overlay, despite 17% QoQ disbursement growth to INR1,306 crores.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a repair-and-transformation year: tighter underwriting, portfolio diversification away from MHCV, opex cuts under Project Leap, and legacy security receipt (SR) clean-up. Q4 disbursements rose 17% QoQ and 21% YoY to INR1,306 crores, and AUM reached INR8,056 crores, up 5% QoQ. Q4 was loss-making because of an additional INR326 crores provision on SRs, a INR49 crores management overlay for West Asia risk, and about INR55 crores of extra ECL charge from the annual model refresh. Management guided to a 3-year framework through FY29 with 35% disbursement CAGR, PAT of INR450-500 crores, and a loan book of INR16,000-17,000 crores.

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements INR1,254 crores (+15% QoQ from INR1,087 crores) at 17.2% yield; AUM over INR7,500 crores. MHCV share of disbursements cut to 31% in FY26 from 57% in FY24, while passenger vehicles rose to 23% from 8%.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements INR52 crores (+73% QoQ from INR30 crores) at 21.8% yield; AUM INR175 crores. Average ticket about INR7.5 lakh, LTV below 40%, tenure about 7 years; 1+ DPD at 0.3%. Live in 108 branches.

segments.name: Security Receipts (legacy)
segments.commentary: Balance sheet SRs of INR1,608 crores from an original pool of INR2,086 crores; about INR470 crores (around 30%) recovered. Additional INR326 crores provision lifts coverage to about 63%, leaving net carrying value about INR589 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY29 targets: 35% CAGR in disbursements, PAT of INR450-500 crores, loan book of INR16,000-17,000 crores; management said the PAT target is for FY29, not FY27.
Normalized credit cost of 2-2.25% once the old book runs off (earlier stated as 2-2.5%); Stage 3 to stabilize at 3.75-4%.
Plans to add about 100 branches over three years; productivity gains of 10-15% per portfolio; opex to rise only marginally in FY27.
April plus expected May FY27 disbursements tracking about 40%+ YoY; Project Leap savings of INR51 crores annualized, INR27 crores realized in FY26.
Micro LAP to launch in at least 2 more states in FY27; target yield about 20% for at least 12-24 months.
SR cash flows expected over roughly 18-36 months; redemptions on large construction projects to start after 12-15 months.
Management overlay of INR49 crores to be held for about 12 months.
capex_capacity: Frontline sales force expanded 30% in H2 FY26 to about 1,600 at 31 March 2026, now about 1,700.
Network of 454 branches across 24 states and UTs (described elsewhere as 23 states); about 5,000 employees.
Micro LAP live in 108 branches of the 454; calibrated rollout planned.
Digital adoption at 84% in vehicle finance and near 100% in Micro LAP; VF lead-to-disbursement TAT cut 25%; eKYC approval received.
Strategic focus limited to vehicle finance and Micro LAP for the next 3 years.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield 17.2% in vehicle finance; management says targeted yield of about 17%+ supports 2-2.25% normalized credit cost.
Customers with CIBIL above 725 rose to 79-80% from 63% in FY24; New-to-Credit exposure fell to 4% from 13%.
New-underwriting book about 60% of portfolio; expected 75% by September 2026 quarter.
Non-starter rate (0+ DPD disbursed in last 6 months) fell to 1.05% from 3.29%.
Micro LAP: management says 20% yield holds for loans up to INR10-12 lakh; loans above INR15 lakh still show about 19% IRR.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further provisioning on the SR book, and when will the construction-project SRs roll off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stressed assets are largely provided for. SR net carrying value of INR589 crores is expected to be realized over about 18-36 months, with redemptions on large construction projects starting after 12-15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the additional INR490 crore buffer (INR326 crores SR plus INR49 crores overlay plus about INR55 crores ECL refresh)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the SR provision as prudence, the INR49 crores overlay as an anticipatory West Asia buffer, and the ECL refresh as revised LGD and PD inputs. It said no stress is visible in the portfolio and that the overlay will be held for about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stage 3 aspiration, and is a 2-2.5% credit cost achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 3 is expected to settle at 3.75-4%, with a gradual decline through the year. Normalized credit cost is targeted at 2-2.25% once the old book runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Are slippages coming mainly from the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed. It said old-cohort delinquency is falling month on month across buckets and that bounce rates are declining.

qa_highlights.question: How is opex expected to behave with disbursements growing 35-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects opex to rise only marginally in FY27, with AUM and revenue growing much faster than costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR450-500 crore PAT target for FY27 or FY29, and does it assume a 2% credit cost and 9% funding cost?
qa_highlights.answer: It is for FY29. Management said it reflects the current 9% incremental borrowing cost and the 2-2.25% normalized credit cost, and that these are not base or worst case. Rating upgrade could lower funding costs further.

risks_watch: Credit quality: gross Stage 3 rose to 4.8% and Q4 slippages were high; the old book is still a large share until about September 2026.
Fuel price increases and West Asia crisis could hit SRTO and fleet customers; management has a INR49 crores overlay and says it would tighten policy if stress appears.
SR recovery timing (18-36 months) and the INR589 crores net carrying value depend on construction-project progress.
Growth ramp versus 35% CAGR target and 100-branch expansion; execution and cost discipline must hold while opex is kept flat.
Management declined to give Q4/Q3 interest reversal and NPA amounts on the call, so interest income flatness is not yet explained.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, funding cost and portfolio trends, with explicit forward targets. More cautious on the macro: it says no stress is visible but has built a buffer. Evasive on the interest-reversal question, which it deferred to a follow-up.
key_quotes: We do expect that this provision will remove the SRs from the list of considerations investors have as they evaluate IndoStar.
And as old book runs out, you would start seeing us stabilizing around 2% to 2.5% credit cost, which is what we're targeting as our yield is about 17% plus.
And if that were to happen, we will tighten our policies and choose portfolio quality over growth in the short term.
